title: Harden JWK/JWS parsing and remove fragile native OpenSSL shim
creator: Priya Rao
description: This ticket consolidates a set of security-focused refactors: replace the brittle native OpenSSL shim used by the SSO/JWK loading path with a pure-Go safe JWK/JWS parser, tighten JWK key validation (reject non-conforming RSA parameters and dubious alg claims), and backport critical CVE patches where upstream fixes are not yet available. Goal is to remove JNI/native symbol dependencies that cause transitive binary compatibility issues, enable a FIPS-compatible build matrix, and add end-to-end SSO preflight tests so regressions are visible in CI.
comments: 2025-11-05 - Spike completed: identified two parsing edge cases in upstream go-jose and one unsafe use of C-level OpenSSL RSA padding in the shim. Notes: https://drive.redwood.com/notes/crypto-spike-jwk-parser

2025-11-10 - Prototyped pure-Go JWK loader that rejects RSA keys with missing 'n' or 'e' or with leading zero padding anomalies. Benchmark: prototype is ~12% slower for cold parse but removes native dependency. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1234

2025-11-18 - Security review kickoff with secops. Raised requirement for deterministic canonicalization of JWK before signature verification to avoid signature stripping CVEs. Action: add test vectors from IETF and internal incident reproducer.

2025-11-26 - Engineering review: identified a place where downstream runtime still calls into the shim for legacy SAML adapters. Added migration sub-issue ENG-77456 to refactor adapters to new loader.
2025-12-01 - PR opened to remove shim and add compatibility layer for older tenants: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1308 - awaiting CI stability on AMD FIPS image.
test_plan: Unit tests for strict JWK key validation (malformed RSA modulus, missing exponent, unexpected kty/alg combos)
Fuzz harness for JWK/JWS parsing to catch unexpected token sequences
Integration SSO flow against staging IdP including signature verification round-trips
Back-compat smoke test matrix that runs legacy SAML adapters against the new loader (see ENG-77456)
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature branch behind feature flag; deploy to staging containers
2) Run canary on non-production tenants for 48h with increased sampling and synthetic auth traffic
3) If canary stable, enable for <10% production traffic with realtime SLO monitoring
4) Gradual ramp to 100% over 7 days; monitor error rates and latency closely and have rollback prepared
5) Post-rollout: run dependency scan and produce final audit note for Compliance
risks: Short-term increase in token-parse latency due to additional validation; mitigations: micro-batching and cache parsed keys
Compatibility break for very old SAML adapters relying on shim behavior; mitigations: compatibility adapter and staged migration (ENG-77456)
FIPS build failures on certain AMI images; mitigation: add FIPS build to CI and run nightly smoke tests
